note: Second Nemotron Nano 9B v2 data point, Q4_K_M this time (bartowski's HF repo, pulled directly via `ollama pull hf.co/...`), for comparison against ollama__nemotron-nano-9b-v2-q4kl__Q4_K_L__8192__1.json. Expectation going in: Q4_K_M is a smaller quant (community/HF card figures put it around 5.51 GB) and should leave enough headroom on this 8 GB card to become fully GPU-resident at num_ctx=8192, unlike the Q4_K_L run. NOT CONFIRMED: this specific bartowski build loads at 6.5 GB (matching this file's on-disk size, not the ~5.51 GB figure researched earlier -- quant-size labels are not fully comparable across repos/maintainers), and gen_tok_s=12.9 is statistically indistinguishable from Q4_K_L's 12.7 tok/s. `ollama ps`'s CPU/GPU split was not captured live for this run (checked seconds too late, after Ollama's idle-unload had already evicted the model) -- the near-identical generation speed to the confirmed-partial-offload Q4_K_L run is circumstantial, not confirmed, evidence that this quant ALSO spills. This is is_cold=true (this model had never been loaded before this call) which folds a genuine first-load cost into load_ms; is_cold is NOT what makes gen_tok_s slow, since gen_tok_s is measured after load completes -- but it does explain why load_ms=128200 is so much larger than this file's Qwen model-switch figures (17-30s): those measured warm switches between already-downloaded Qwen sizes, not a genuinely cold first load of a 6.5 GB file plus whatever Nemotron's hybrid Mamba-2 architecture costs to initialize that a plain transformer does not pay. Re-running this exact call now that the model is warm, and confirming the CPU/GPU split via `ollama ps` polled DURING generation rather than after, is the natural next data point -- not yet taken.
